unit.why: A first-person memorate, quoted from the manuscript Megillat Setarim, in which a starving child is sent by his tsaddik father to a tavern and is fed by a 'gentile' later understood to be Elijah.
unit.boundary_note: Fuller variant of the story told in the previous division ('סיפור הנ"ל מאות ה׳'), but it stands on its own.

stories.start_quote: בכ״י קונטרס מגלת סתרים מבנו מורינו
stories.summary_en: The tsaddik's young son, starving after a day without food, is told by his father to go to a tavern-keeper who would never give him credit; a gentile sitting there offers him bread and brandy, and the father later explains that it was Elijah, seen only in this confused way because of the boy's sins.

quotes: שמגודל עונותי לא זכיתי לראות אליהו
tags.why: The disguised gentile is revealed to be Elijah.

quotes: ואמר לי אבי לך אל השכינת
tags.why: The tsaddik's son is the narrator and protagonist, and the father acts.

quotes: לך אל השכינת וקח לך לאכול
tags.why: The female tavern-keeper (שינקערין) is the destination; she is referred to but does not act.

quotes: רוצה אתה לחם ונתן לי הכל
tags.why: The boy is miraculously fed by a stranger.
The father knows in advance and explains the hidden identity of the stranger.

quotes: לך אל השכינת וקח לך לאכול
tags.why: The father's instruction implies a prediction that the boy will be fed, which comes true.

quotes: לא הי' לי פנאי להשכיל מה זאת
tags.why: Only afterwards does the boy realize that the gentile was Elijah.

quotes: וישב שם גוי ותיכף אמר אלי
tags.why: The boy is fed by an apparent gentile.
Brandy is offered and given to the boy.

quotes: והאמנתי בו והלכתי ועמדתי על הפתח
tags.why: The son trusts his father's instruction against all expectation.
The tavern-keeper woman is only referred to.

missing_concepts: hunger / starvation of the tsaddik's family
the child of a tsaddik as narrator (first-person memorate from a manuscript)
seeing Elijah in a degraded form because of one's sins
